title: Pervasive defensive-hedge writing across multiple sections
description: 5 distinct defensive-hedge constructions (e.g. "we do not claim …", "not X but rather Y") across 3 non-excluded sections (body, introduction, method). The text repeatedly defends against anticipated objections instead of directly stating what was done — a common AI writing-style tell that lowers information density. This is a STYLE IMPRESSION with ZERO verdict weight, not a factual inconsistency and not an authorship verdict. If a specific hedge instead reveals a real scope/evaluation limitation, that is a separate integrity finding (HP-SCOPE-INFLATE / eval-design-forensics).

evidence.span: We do not claim that this routing module is optimal.
This does not mean that simpler designs cannot work.
We are not proposing a fundamentally new architecture.

fp_case: Some venues / AI reviewers penalize the ABSENCE of caveats, so measured hedging is a legitimate strategic choice; a single scoping sentence is not the pattern.
recommended_reviewer_action: Skim the cited sentences: if the paper over-hedges in its contribution/body, that lowers readability. Impression only — not misconduct, not an authorship judgment.
